title: Smallest Word With Every Letter Once

concept.title: Keep the stack increasing, but never lose the last copy of a letter
body: You must choose a subsequence of the word that contains **each distinct letter exactly once** and is as small as possible in alphabetical order. A greedy idea: we want small letters early. When a new letter `ch` arrives, a bigger letter on top of the stack can be **popped** (replaced by the smaller `ch`) if that bigger letter occurs **again later** in the word, because then it is not lost.

Prepare `last[c]`, the position of the last occurrence of every letter. Keep a stack and a set `in_stack`. For each position `i` with letter `ch`: if `ch` is already in the stack, skip it. Otherwise pop while the top is bigger than `ch` **and** its last occurrence is after `i`; then push `ch`.
Each letter is pushed and popped a limited number of times, so the loop is linear. The answer is the content of the stack.

statement: Given a word of lowercase letters, find the lexicographically smallest word that is a subsequence of it and contains every different letter of the word exactly once. Print that word.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.

examples.note: The letters are a, b, c, d: the smallest word is acdb.

hints: Remember the last position of each letter.
Skip a letter that is already in the stack.
Pop bigger letters from the top while they appear again later.

explanation: A bigger letter on top of the stack is replaced by a smaller new letter only if the bigger one occurs again later. Letters already in the stack are skipped.
